headline: Medium-risk pair: shared file-based workflows can enable prompt injection and data leakage; no direct evidence of tighter coupling.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Plane can ingest file uploads and issue/task content, while system_prompts_leaks is a prompt-leakage-oriented source-available project. A shared filesystem or manual handoff could let attacker-controlled content from B influence A’s task handling. No direct bridge is documented, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF the two agents exchange content through a shared workspace or copied files, prompt-like text from B can reach A.
IF A treats uploaded file contents as trusted instructions, injected text can influence task handling.
mitigations: Disable shared folders between the agents.
Strip instruction-like text from uploaded files before A processes them.
Use a human review step for any B-generated content before it enters A.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for all cross-agent artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Plane touches issues, tasks, roadmaps, files, images, hyperlinks, and notes, and has broad network egress; B is source-available but shows no egress. If sensitive Plane data is copied into B or if A forwards file contents externally, leakage is plausible. The pair lacks documented isolation, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF Plane data classes such as files or notes are copied into B, those contents may be exposed outside the original workspace.
IF A forwards uploaded file contents over the network, sensitive task data can leave the local environment.
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive files in shared locations.
Turn off or restrict A’s outbound network destinations.
Use separate accounts and workspaces for each agent.
Redact files before any cross-agent transfer.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention rules.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no filesystem write capability and B exposes no write or network capability, so direct write-write contention is not evident. The only plausible overlap is indirect through shared files or operator-mediated transfers, which makes conflict possible but limited. Because no locking or shared mutable resource is documented, low is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable workspace through external orchestration, they can contend over shared artifacts.
IF an operator copies outputs between them without versioning, stale overwrites can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate directories to each agent.
Use read-only handoff files.
Keep one writer per artifact.
Add timestamps to transferred outputs.
requires-engineering: add file locking or optimistic concurrency control.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Plane produces issues, tasks, and roadmaps that can be treated as authoritative work products, while B’s project name and docs suggest prompt-leakage content that could be forwarded as input. If B consumes A’s outputs without verification, errors can cascade into downstream decisions. No built-in verification step is documented, so medium fits.
conditions: IF B uses Plane-generated tasks or roadmaps as authoritative input, any upstream mistake propagates downstream.
IF an operator forwards A’s outputs into B without review, B may amplify incorrect assumptions.
mitigations: Require manual verification before B consumes A outputs.
Limit B to summarizing rather than acting on A’s content.
Mark A outputs as untrusted until checked.
Use a checklist for cross-agent handoffs.
requires-engineering: add validation gates between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Plane explicitly handles files and notes and offers self-hosted deployment, while B is source-available with no stated residency or retention controls. There is no direct evidence of a residency mismatch or regulated data class, so compliance risk is limited to policy gaps rather than a clear breach pathway. The absence of B controls is noted but not enough for higher severity.
conditions: IF regulated data is stored in Plane and then exported to B, local policy may be violated.
IF B is deployed without retention controls, operator-defined compliance rules may be harder to enforce.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of cross-agent workflows.
Document retention rules for both agents.
Use self-hosted Plane only for compliant datasets.
Review export paths before sharing content.
requires-engineering: implement residency and retention enforcement.
